context_documents.title: 2024-3478 · Consistent staging is needed before a multi-pose launcher can be accurate
context_documents.body:
# 2024-3478: Consistent staging is needed before a multi-pose launcher can be accurate

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A roller collector feeds a compliant-wheel launcher that rises on an elevator for amp and trap. Three distance sensors establish note position; magnetic switches protect climb travel. Trap execution changes hooks, elevator height and launcher angle in a defined sequence.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly connects the distance sensors to placing the note consistently and the limit devices to preventing mechanism damage. More exact intake material/ratio details are not established by the selected caption passages.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

One launcher serving several targets reduces duplicate release hardware but changes gravity, retention and moving mass across poses. A correct angle table assumes a repeatable note position. The climb/trap sequence must also avoid moving the launcher through the chain or frame while partially loaded.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test staged-note position spread, sensor disagreement and retention during elevator motion. Validate the complete trap sequence with realistic swing and lateral approach error.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/cXPduxI0fCU](https://youtu.be/cXPduxI0fCU)

source_reviews.title: FIRST 2024 team record
facts: The registered robot is Michelangelo. The team won Bayou and was a Newton division finalist.
source_reviews.limitations: Awards and alliance results do not verify a mechanism.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers interview announcement
facts: The publisher identifies the linked episode as a 3478 robot walkthrough.
source_reviews.limitations: The introduction gives no construction or mechanism chronology.

source_reviews.title: LamBot Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.locator: Inherited corpus robot dossier and focused study
source_reviews.review_basis: Older dossier only. Direct caption retrieval failed in this review.
facts: The inherited study describes a deployed pickup, a sensor-staged pivoting launcher and an elevator used for amp and trap.
The inherited study describes rearward relocation of the hooks and a change in intake contact material.
source_reviews.limitations: The interview's full readable captions were not obtained. Treat its reported mechanism details as inherited.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The inherited architecture places a pivoted scorer on a lift. A floor pickup and intervening transfer supply a note for a speaker shot in the lower configuration or for raised placement. The distinctive coupling is in endgame. The dossier says the hook location was moved to influence how the chassis hangs near the trap. If that account is confirmed, the static pose of the hanging chassis is part of the placement mechanism.
piece_flow: The roller collector gathers a floor note and supplies the transfer.
Distance sensing is reported to establish a staging point before launch. The sensor count and the exact state sequence remain unverified.
The pivot sets release geometry. The lift changes exit height for amp or trap in the inherited description.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The lift, launcher and hanging geometry should be drawn as a single system. A hook change can move the entire release point relative to the trap. The direction and size of that displacement depend on the loaded center of mass, chain geometry and whether the chassis is in contact with the stage. A floor-based clearance drawing will miss those differences.

subsystems.name: Pickup and staging
subsystems.construction: Inherited roller collector and intervening roller path with distance sensing.
subsystems.operation: Gather a floor note and stop it at a repeatable point before release.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older dossier reports a material change for grip.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: More grip is useful only if the transfer can take the note without dragging its rim or folding it. Compare off-center pickups and worn notes before changing the roller material.
subsystems.interfaces: Deployment clearance, overlapping roller capture and sensing across the open center of the note.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed check: log where a partially caught or skewed note actually stops and whether reversal can recover it.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller material, sensor geometry and jam logic.

subsystems.name: Elevator and chain hooks
subsystems.construction: Inherited description of a pivoted wheel launcher on an elevator and independently operated hooks.
subsystems.operation: Raise the scorer for placement and use chain engagement to reach the hanging pose.
subsystems.team_rationale: Inherited description attributes rearward hook relocation to improved hanging orientation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Hook placement can remove the need for another powered placement joint if its hanging pose is repeatable. An asymmetric catch or a changed battery position can shift that pose.
subsystems.interfaces: The raised carriage must clear the chain and hooks with the note present. The hooks must keep the robot stable before the release.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed checks: loaded one-sided catch and access to a stalled elevator. Inspect the hook mounts for a load path independent of the scoring carriage.
subsystems.unknowns: Hook offsets, leveling logic, chain contact and success rates.

revisions: Intake contact material and hook position changed according to the older dossier. Event boundaries remain open.
transferable_principles: Use the loaded endgame pose as a design input. Verify the landing window for the note under variations in chain position and carriage pose.
disconfirming_conditions: Transfer weakens if the chain pose varies more than the trap entry tolerates or if a higher scoring carriage moves the suspended center of mass enough to consume alignment margin.
remaining_gaps: Full interview captions or a team write-up, elevator section, staging/reversal sequence and calibrated views of the loaded hook-to-trap geometry.
recommended_images: Interview frame showing the launcher and elevator at a known position
Side view of a loaded hang with hook line and trap entrance visible
